import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/test_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/test_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/test_3.csv"
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/test_4.csv"

# Load all source dataframes
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs'] (516 rows)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs'] (516 rows)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs'] (516 rows)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs'] (516 rows)
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs'] (258 rows)

# Step 1: Aggregate df0 by batsman summing batsman_runs (to align with target batsman_runs_x)
agg0 = df0.groupby('batsman', as_index=False)['batsman_runs'].sum()
agg0.rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_x'}, inplace=True)

# Step 2: Aggregate df1 by batsman summing total_runs (to align with total_runs_x)
agg1 = df1.groupby('batsman', as_index=False)['total_runs'].sum()
agg1.rename(columns={'total_runs': 'total_runs_x'}, inplace=True)

# Step 3: Aggregate df2 by batsman summing total_runs (to align with total_runs_y)
agg2 = df2.groupby('batsman', as_index=False)['total_runs'].sum()
agg2.rename(columns={'total_runs': 'total_runs_y'}, inplace=True)

# Step 4: Aggregate df3 by batsman summing batsman_runs (to align with batsman_runs_y)
agg3 = df3.groupby('batsman', as_index=False)['batsman_runs'].sum()
agg3.rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_y'}, inplace=True)

# Step 5: df4 already has 258 rows and columns ['batsman', 'batsman_runs'] which corresponds to the final 'batsman_runs' column in target
# Rename batsman_runs to 'batsman_runs' (final column)
df4_renamed = df4.rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs'})

# Step 6: Merge all aggregated dataframes on 'batsman'
# Start merging agg0 and agg1
merged = pd.merge(agg0, agg1, on='batsman', how='outer')
# Merge with agg2
merged = pd.merge(merged, agg2, on='batsman', how='outer')
# Merge with agg3
merged = pd.merge(merged, agg3, on='batsman', how='outer')
# Merge with df4_renamed (final batsman_runs)
merged = pd.merge(merged, df4_renamed, on='batsman', how='inner')  # inner join to keep only batsmen present in df4 (258 rows)

# Step 7: Fill NaNs with appropriate types
# batsman_runs_x is float, total_runs_x/y and batsman_runs_y are integers, batsman_runs is integer
merged['batsman_runs_x'] = merged['batsman_runs_x'].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
merged['total_runs_x'] = merged['total_runs_x'].fillna(0).astype(int)
merged['total_runs_y'] = merged['total_runs_y'].fillna(0).astype(int)
merged['batsman_runs_y'] = merged['batsman_runs_y'].fillna(0).astype(int)
merged['batsman_runs'] = merged['batsman_runs'].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Step 8: Reorder columns to match target schema
final_df = merged[['batsman', 'batsman_runs_x', 'total_runs_x', 'total_runs_y', 'batsman_runs_y', 'batsman_runs']]

# Step 9: Write the final dataframe to the target CSV path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_33/target_multisource_cot.csv"
final_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
